results.content:
## Your Gut Is Probably Right. Here's What to Look For:

If you're trying to figure out whether someone is worth trusting online, here are a few things to look out for:

 Every problem leads to a supplement
 Lots of scientific-sounding language, but nothing is ever clearly explained
 "Personalized" plans sold en masse
 Speaking in absolutes (this "always" works or "never" eat this!)
 Normal symptoms framed as major dysfunction
 Constant talk of hormones, cortisol, toxins, or inflammation
 You're made to feel broken, deficient, or damaged before being offered a solution
 Everything funnels toward a product

Questions worth asking before you buy: [...] ## When Is AI Useful vs. When Is It Dishonest?

This isn't an "AI bad, humans are good" conversation. As always, there is much more nuance than that! As personalized, evidence-based nutrition coaches at KLN we have a very strong, clear AI Policy that dictates how we use artificial intelligence (and most importantly, how we don’t). I think the line from helpful to harmful can be crossed when:

 Chat GPT-generated plans are sold as real, personalized coaching
 Generic advice is presented as tailored to you
 Content is posted that the creator doesn't actually understand
 Fake testimonials or fake results are used
 AI use is hidden because the creator knows people would trust them less
 AI is used to make someone look more qualified than they are [...] Skip to Content

# The Fitness Industry Has an AI Problem

HTF Podcast

Written By Kate Lyman

This post is based on our latest podcast episode diving deep into the world of AI in the fitness industry — from fake personas to mass-produced meal plans. Listen to the full episode for the full conversation!

## Is the Real Problem AI… or the Fitness Industry?

The fitness and wellness space has always rewarded a lot of the wrong things, like mistaking a lean figure for knowledge and expertise.

Now add tools that let anyone mass-produce content, manufacture authority, and (in some cases) create an entirely fake person to deliver it all, and the online space has become even harder to navigate.

results.title: How I Used AI to Get Back In Shape and Lose 30 Pounds - Consumer Reports
results.content:
About six weeks later, that’s exactly what happened.

Throughout November and December, I was checking in with both tools after workouts, after weigh-ins, and whenever something felt off. When I reported that my scale weight was barely moving, but my lifts were going up and my waist was visibly shrinking, Gemini explained the underlying math: If you burn 10 pounds of fat while simultaneously adding five pounds of muscle, the scale only moves five pounds—but your body has fundamentally changed.

“You are trading fluff for armor. This is the Holy Grail scenario.”

The “fluff for armor” line sounded a little over the top, but that’s AI for you: eager to please. [...] I’m neither an AI evangelist nor a blind skeptic. AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude are resources I use often to make routine tasks a touch easier and more fun. So it felt natural to consult an AI platform or two to help me formulate my fitness plan.

I know some folks will object to the way I approached this exercise, bristling at health metrics like BMI and the scope of my interactions with a widely unpredictable technology, but I’m not a health expert and certainly not advocating that you mirror what I did. I’m just curious about AI and eager to explore what it can do. [...] And, finally, she endorses the practice of logging your behavior—food, exercise, sleep—and periodically uploading that data to AI for review. “You can go back weeks later and say, ‘Here’s what I’ve been doing. What suggestions do you have?’” As the journey progresses, she adds, the relationship with the AI naturally evolves: At the beginning, it’s about building a program; later, it can help you troubleshoot plateaus, stay motivated, or find ways to fit fitness into a changing schedule.
